## ACL-1768 re-review (round 3): PR #833 @ 6bd043df (Reviewer-AS1025AU) — APPROVED

main is still 4c63ef0c; the PR base is 4c63ef0c and the PR is MERGEABLE. The diff vs main has 22 files, 1768-only: no targeting_resolver.py / test_acl1771 changes, so the 1771 code now comes from main.

### Merge 74eb343a vs my merge notes
I rebuilt my resolved trial tree (main + my resolution) and compared it with 74eb343a. The `src` difference is limited to a removed comment, the order of the copy_more/file_vertical lines in app.py, and an en-dash in a JS comment. tests/test_acl1819_preflight.py adds the new 2-ad-set texts_dynamic parity fixtures. - the Primary-text-2 RPA refusal is dropped;
- TermResolver gets cache/scope; API_ONLY_SLOT_KEYS is the union of both sides;
- FUTURE = placements + copyTo; `_targeting_body` is defined once;
- 1774's more_copy_names/vertical_filename are set per ad set.

### Blockers from round 2: fixed
1. **Targeting reads.** `estimate_targeting_reads` = min(90, 6 + 6 × distinct terms and parts across all sets) is added to the per-campaign budget. The write-refusal threshold stays at 250, and the env ceiling is 250+90. I reran my FakeMeta repro (10 sets × 3 ads × 3 work-position terms, cold cache): budget 330, 252 calls used, success. With 4 terms per set the resolver cap is hit and the run is refused before any write ("press Check plan again"); this is 1771 behaviour. 2 sets × 3 terms: success.
2. **ACL-1891.** `_prepare` refuses before the first write when `chunk_calls + estimate_create_calls(plan) > budget`. Check plan (`writing=False`) keeps the old reserve. The 1891 test is rewritten and a new test is added; the 1891 suite passes.

### Non-blocking items from round 2: done
- The pixel guard is dropped.
- Targeting of all ad sets is resolved before one combined TargetingUnresolved is raised.
- A comment now covers creative numbering.
- The changelog covers the v3-page downgrade.

### Remaining notes (non-blocking, no re-review needed)
- **Remaining-budget comment is inaccurate.** The comments say "if writes don't fit after the reads, `_prepare` refuses before the first write". The code only checks when there are large-video chunks. For non-video plans, the targeting reserve is the only guard. One edge: the resolver is shared across campaigns of one job, and its job cap is cumulative (`len(_results)`), so a later campaign can in theory read more than its own reserve. Cheap hardening for a follow-up: an unconditional `client.max_calls - client.calls < estimate_create_calls(plan)` refusal at the end of `_prepare` when writing.
- **The concurrent-confirm test failure is not a lock race.** The 1771 test `test_concurrent_confirms_do_not_lose_entries` (11 == 12 under load) passes in my full group run and in 150 extra 12-thread loops. `ConfirmedStore.put` holds `_STORE_LOCK` around read → modify → atomic replace, so in-process writes are serialized. The likely cause is a transient Windows file-sharing error (AV/indexer) on `os.replace` or `_read`.
  - It does expose a real 1771 robustness gap, so I suggest a follow-up task for 1771 (not this PR):
    - `_read` maps any OSError, including PermissionError, to `{}`, and the next `put` would then rewrite the file with only the new entry, dropping the confirmed cache;
    - `os.replace` is not retried.
  - Fix: on a read error other than file-not-found, refuse to write or retry, and retry the replace on PermissionError.

The write-refusal threshold stays at 250, and the env ceiling is 250+90. I reran my FakeMeta repro (10 sets × 3 ads × 3 work-position terms, cold cache): budget 330, 252 calls used, success. With 4 terms per set the resolver cap is hit and the run is refused before any write ("press Check plan again"); this is 1771 behaviour. 2 sets × 3 terms: success.

- **Remaining-budget comment is inaccurate.** The comments say "if writes don't fit after the reads, `_prepare` refuses before the first write". The code only checks when there are large-video chunks. For non-video plans, the targeting reserve is the only guard. One edge: the resolver is shared across campaigns of one job, and its job cap is cumulative (`len(_results)`), so a later campaign can in theory read more than its own reserve. Cheap hardening for a follow-up: an unconditional `client.max_calls - client.calls < estimate_create_calls(plan)` refusal at the end of `_prepare` when writing.
- **The concurrent-confirm test failure is not a lock race.** The 1771 test `test_concurrent_confirms_do_not_lose_entries` (11 == 12 under load) passes in my full group run and in 150 extra 12-thread loops. `ConfirmedStore.put` holds `_STORE_LOCK` around read → modify → atomic replace, so in-process writes are serialized. The likely cause is a transient Windows file-sharing error (AV/indexer) on `os.replace` or `_read`.
  - It does expose a real 1771 robustness gap, so I suggest a follow-up task for 1771 (not this PR):
    - `_read` maps any OSError, including PermissionError, to `{}`, and the next `put` would then rewrite the file with only the new entry, dropping the confirmed cache;

## Findings (to fix)
1. **Release of a profile held on another machine/user (blocking).** warm.py:1065-1068 calls `_start_after_lock` for any message containing "lock profile". The RPA path it mirrors refuses to release when MLX says the profile is held elsewhere (`_start_held_elsewhere(msg)`, src/fb_ads_rpa/browser.py:2379 and :2569, "not ours to unlock"). The API path lacks that guard, and `profile_run_state` returns "stopped" for a profile absent from the LOCAL statuses (multilogin_launcher.py:228-229) — exactly the case when someone runs it on another computer. Result: ACL sends a stop for a profile a person is using elsewhere. 2. **The wait holds shared places (other accounts affected).** `_start_after_lock` runs inside the job queue slot (`grant`) and the job start turn (`_starting`, ACL-2283 one-at-a-time), so for up to 120 s other accounts' starts wait behind this locked profile. Fix: give back the slot/turn while waiting (or wait before taking them, like `_wait_until_closed` at warm.py:970-978), then take them again for the single retry. Add a test that another profile's start is not blocked during the wait.
3. Minor: when the wait ends because of Stop (`cancelled()`), the account shows "Multilogin still holds ..." (`profile_locked`) instead of the usual cancelled result. Cosmetic: `else:` body at warm.py:1078-1079 indented 24 spaces.

src/fb_api/stop_reason.py:38-39 `reason_failure` treats any stored account status other than ""/"clear" as a Meta-given reason, including "unknown" (stored by account_spend._read_status / account_spend_api.map_status when a read learned nothing). Reproduced on head: a tab_unresponsive stop on an account whose stored status is "unknown" shows "Meta reports a problem with this ad account - check it in Ads Manager, then Publish again" instead of "The Ads Manager tab stopped answering - Publish again". The same gate (reason_failure_known) makes publish_jobs.apply_account_signal rewrite stopped rows on every later "unknown" write. Fails criterion 2 / owner rule "never invent reasons".

Fix: return None for status in ("", "clear", "unknown") and add a test with a stored "unknown" status (test_acl2811_publish_stop_reason.py:49 only covers an empty store). Consider ignoring statuses get_status marks stale. Non-blocking: creator.py:1982 MSG_BUSY still says "Wait for it to finish".

ACL-2816 passed integration review and ships without 2811.

1738.review_report:
# Review return ACL-2738 (PR #1739, head b5daa8747)

Independent review of PR #1739 (1896ea348..b5daa8747) against Issue #1738 (ACL-2738, ACL-2668 decision 16). Verdict: changes requested. The wait itself is correct: the 300 s / 20-poll cap and the video_timeout stop are gone, live_progress shows Meta's percent and elapsed time, there is a step plus beat plus waiting=video_processing for the silence watcher (signal only, it never kills), video_status=error stops with kind video_error and Meta's phase reason, and the resume check (_prepare) now stops only on error. Things I confirmed: (a) Restarting while the video is processing works. A scratch probe cancelled run 1 after 2 processing polls, and run 2 reused the same video (no second upload, it was found by tag or journal), waited and created both ads. (b) max_calls: polls past CALLS_PER_VIDEO_POLLS add +1 to client.max_calls under an isinstance(int) guard, so the net cost is zero against _chunk_spare. It is compatible with PR #1731 (ACL-2687, max_calls=None), and PR #1648 (ACL-2644) does not touch _wait_video. Note: #1731 edits the same PROJECT.md line 387, so expect a textual conflict for whichever merges second. Blocking findings: (1) CI red, caused by this PR. linux tests shard 3 fails tests/test_acl1775_instant_forms.py::test_website_plan_posts_and_readback_are_identical_to_the_pre_forms_creator (line 694). The golden steps now contain the new step 'ad 2: video processing at Meta - waiting until it is ready' (creator.py _wait_video, the _step(...) when announced). Either drop that step from out.steps (live_progress already shows it) or filter it in the golden comparison. ACL verification fails as a consequence. (2) Cancel does not really stop the wait in the slow phase. After 20 polls the creator sleeps VIDEO_POLL_MAX_S=60 s with the injected sleep, which in production is plain time.sleep (publish_api.py:377, passed at :824), so Cancel is seen only after up to 60 s plus the GET. publish_jobs.CANCEL_DEADLINE_S is also 60 s (publish_jobs.py:65, _enforce_cancel_deadline). A Cancel during a long wait therefore regularly hits _abandon_job: the job is marked 'the robot was stuck in ...', and the profile lock stays held until the thread wakes. The new cancel test uses sleep=lambda s: None and cannot catch this. Fix: a cancel-aware sleep (sleep in slices of 1-2 s and check self.cancelled()), or a slow interval well below the cancel deadline, plus a test with a real clock or sleep that asserts cancel lands within a few seconds. (3) The endless wait has no exit for terminal non-error states. Only 'ready' and 'error' end the loop (creator.py _wait_video). Meta's video_status also has 'expired' (an upload that will never become ready), and an empty or missing status also loops forever. A scratch probe with video_status='expired' polled 500 times and ended only by Cancel. In production that holds the job's profile slot (profile_slots ceiling or memory) forever and can starve the publish queue for other accounts, against the rule that a problem on one account is shown on that account only. Fix: treat 'expired' (and a phase status=='error' even when video_status is not 'error') as terminal, stopping the ad with Meta's reason, and add a test. Non-blocking: the progress line could also include Meta's phase name. Tests at b5daa8747 (PYTHONUTF8=1, PYTHONPATH=tests): test_acl1761_api_create, test_acl1856_operation_journal, test_acl1891_video_chunks, test_acl2639_resumable_upload, test_acl1768_ad_sets, test_acl1774_texts_vertical = 645 passed. The scratch probes (restart mid-processing, expired) gave 2 passed, demonstrating the behaviour above. # ACL-2819 review — Reviewer-R1119A2819 (rev_1119_a2819)

PR #1823, head eacc93ba31ffb7a5c2612a625194be6958a4e547 (tree ba180045c), base = main 355097dfa (compare: ahead).
Verdict: **changes_requested**.

## What is right
- `_start_after_lock` (src/fb_api/warm.py:1103-1122) releases only when local MLX `profile_run_state` returns "stopped"; "running" and None (unknown/unreadable) keep waiting and, at the deadline, return None -> `profile_locked` with no stop call. Treating None as "wait" is safe: no release is ever made on an unknown status.
- Wait is bounded: `CLOSE_WAIT_S` (120 s), polling `CLOSE_POLL_S` (3 s), cancel-aware. Exactly one start retry after one release (test_cant_lock_is_retried_once_only).
- Only local launcher calls (`/profile/statuses`, `/profile/stop/p/{id}`); no Meta/Graph call. The lease (`try_lease`) covers this profile only.
- plain_errors.py:214 now classifies "can't lock profile"/"cannot lock profile" as `profile_locked`.
- Local tests at eacc93ba3 (PYTHONUTF8=1, C:/acl-test-9095q venv): test_acl2262_builder_opens_profile, test_acl1812_warm_sessions, test_acl2268_auto_warm, test_acl2344_warm_light, test_acl2392_plain_errors = 246 passed.

## Findings (to fix)
1. **Release of a profile held on another machine/user (blocking).** warm.py:1065-1068 calls `_start_after_lock` for any message containing "lock profile". The RPA path it mirrors refuses to release when MLX says the profile is held elsewhere (`_start_held_elsewhere(msg)`, src/fb_ads_rpa/browser.py:2379 and :2569, "not ours to unlock"). The API path lacks that guard, and `profile_run_state` returns "stopped" for a profile absent from the LOCAL statuses (multilogin_launcher.py:228-229) — exactly the case when someone runs it on another computer. Result: ACL sends a stop for a profile a person is using elsewhere. Fix: if the start error carries the held-elsewhere marks ("another device/machine/user", "different user"), do not release; return the held-by-another-machine text on that account. Add a test.
2. **The wait holds shared places (other accounts affected).** `_start_after_lock` runs inside the job queue slot (`grant`) and the job start turn (`_starting`, ACL-2283 one-at-a-time), so for up to 120 s other accounts' starts wait behind this locked profile. Acceptance says "no effect on other accounts". Fix: give back the slot/turn while waiting (or wait before taking them, like `_wait_until_closed` at warm.py:970-978), then take them again for the single retry. Add a test that another profile's start is not blocked during the wait.
3. Minor: when the wait ends because of Stop (`cancelled()`), the account shows "Multilogin still holds ..." (`profile_locked`) instead of the usual cancelled result. Cosmetic: `else:` body at warm.py:1078-1079 indented 24 spaces.

CI at review time: windows tests pass; linux shards pending; tracker-link failed. Not approved.

## Round 2 — Worker-W1119N2819B
- Finding 1: warm.py `_held_elsewhere` (same marks as RPA `_start_held_elsewhere`): "can't lock" + another device/machine/user -> profile_locked on the account, no status look, no stop.
- Finding 2: the wait/stop now runs in `_release_after_lock` AFTER the queue slot, start turn and profile lease are given back; open_one loops twice (take turn+slot -> start; on lock: wait -> take them again -> single retry).
- Finding 3: Stop during the wait returns stop_log.CANCELLED_TEXT with code "cancelled"; mis-indented else removed. Unreadable lock status (exception) = unknown = wait.
- New tests (test_acl2262): held-elsewhere never stopped; lock wait holds neither slot nor turn; stop shows cancelled.
- Tests (PYTHONUTF8=1): 2262, 1812, 2283, 2328, 2268, 2392 = 270 passed.

# ACL-2821 review — Reviewer-R1119A2821 (rev_1119_a2821)

PR #1826, head 35f7367dc1955d2a4cfba559e23147031ed593f7 (tree 489ed592c), base = main 355097dfa (compare: ahead).
Verdict: **changes_requested**.

## What is right
- 403/FORBIDDEN_REQUEST is now classified on slot A and slot B (mlx_session.py:124-140); slot A -> mlx_workspace_mismatch.
- Refusals stay per slot: `_MISMATCH`/`stopped` are keyed by instance; slot A accounts keep starting (test_known_mismatch_skips_the_start_and_leaves_the_other_slot_alone, ACL-1826 batch test). No global stop.
- `note_started(slot)` pops the slot from `_MISMATCH` and every batch's stopped/suspect/probing: one success clears it.
- Publish gets one batch id per publisher (publish_api.py:580-583), reads one per read (account_spend_api.py:584). The page's Read-all batch (`ra-`/`rc-`) still latches, because `note_failure` latches every live batch of the slot and `_mlx_batch_refusal` (app.py:4810) checks it before the read starts — no regression.
- JS BATCH_STOPS lists (warm_sessions.js:224, report.html:10553/15222, _campaign_table.html:265) left without mlx_workspace_mismatch: correct. Those lists turn a code into ONE batch line + Retry above the table; leaving the mismatch out keeps it on each account's row, which is what the Issue and the owner rule ("shown on that account only", no new banners) ask for.
- Local tests at 35f7367dc (PYTHONUTF8=1, C:/acl-test-9095q venv): test_acl1826_mlx_session_lost, test_acl2821_workspace_mismatch, test_acl2668_* = 74 passed, 1 failed (test_acl2668_ram_ceiling::test_settings_show_the_effective_machine_value — order-dependent, fails the same way on main 355097dfa in the same combination, passes alone; unrelated).

## Findings (to fix)
1. **The inference overrides ACL-1826 for good and the text states it as fact (blocking).** `classify` returns WORKSPACE_MISMATCH for slot B whenever `_last_ok() == "A"` (mlx_session.py:111-112). `_LAST_OK` is process-wide and never expires; it is only cleared for the slot that got the mismatch (B), never for A. So once any slot-A start succeeded since serve.py started (hours earlier is enough), every later slot-B 403 says "Multilogin app is signed in to Inhouse - switch it to KLD". The real ACL-1826 case — the shared KLD sign-in was taken by another computer while Inhouse keeps working — becomes unreachable on any machine that also has slot-A accounts, and the buyer is told to switch the app, which (if the app really serves both) can break the Inhouse accounts too. There is no direct query of the app's workspace; a 403 plus "A started earlier" does not tell these two apart. Fix (smallest): hedge the text for the inferred case, e.g. "Multilogin refused the KLD profile - the app may be signed in to Inhouse, or the KLD sign-in is in use on another computer. Switch the app to KLD or sign in again here, then press Retry." (and the mirror for slot A); or keep SESSION_LOST unless the A success is recent (same batch / minutes) AND hedge. Update the tests that pin the exact text (test_acl2821_workspace_mismatch TO_KLD/TO_INHOUSE, test_acl1826 B4/B5).
2. **Immediate latch skips the ACL-2668 recheck on that guess.** note_failure sets `checked=True` for WORKSPACE_MISMATCH (mlx_session.py:257-258), so after an A success the first B 403 latches the slot without the one recheck that ACL-2668 gives a lost session. If the inference is wrong (finding 1), a transient refusal now skips the rest of the slot in the batch. Keep the one recheck unless the mismatch is certain.
3. Minor: `note_started` writes `state["app"]` into every live batch (mlx_session.py:281-282), so a slot-A start in another concurrent job counts as "app is in Inhouse" for this batch's skip in `refusal` (mlx_session.py:334-343). Scope it to the batch of the start, or note it as intended.
4. Research on automatic switching (Issue spec) is not in the PR/changelog; add it to the handoff report.

CI: windows tests pass; linux tests 1-3 and ACL verification failed on infrastructure (apt mirror unreachable, "ci_retry: all 3 attempts failed for: python -m playwright install-deps chromium"); tracker-link failed "waiting for the Worker handoff to Review". CI not green. Not approved.

## Round 2 (Worker-W1119N2821B)

Fixes for the review findings:
1. Hedged text. A 403 on slot A (`mlx_workspace_mismatch`) now reads "Multilogin refused to open this Inhouse profile - the Multilogin app may be signed in to KLD (switch it to Inhouse), or the Inhouse sign-in is in use on another computer". Slot B keeps ACL-1826 code `mlx_session_lost` (so its batch banner and Retry behaviour are unchanged) with the mirror text (KLD / Inhouse); the static JS copy in acm_commands.js was updated too. Names come from the slot labels.
